paragraphs: Electro Scan sells leak detection and lead pipe location work for water and sewer systems. The company says municipal sewer utilities and sewer contractors use it to pin down the location, measurement and flow of defects inside a pipe before a repair or replacement job.

The method rests on a simple claim: pipe defects that leak water also leak electricity, so a defect shows up whether or not it happens to be leaking during the inspection. A low voltage conductivity probe travels through the pipe at 45 to 60 feet per minute, locating and measuring defects as it goes. Crews can then create summary and detail level reports for a team to review. The flagship probe is built for gravity mains between 6 and 30 inches in diameter, and the company says agencies and contractors use it worldwide.

Electro Scan lists ISO 9001:2015 certification for quality management systems. Its case studies page includes a North American benchmark study comparing closed-circuit television inspection with focused electrode leak location on gravity sewer mains. Other write-ups describe a Florida utility dealing with excessive inflow and infiltration in its gravity collection system.
